I have completed the reverse-engineering investigation of `cinejoy.pk` for the LG webOS TV application.

### Core Verified Discoveries
1. **Frontend Architecture**: Pure client-side SvelteKit SPA (`_app/immutable/*`) fronted by DDOS-Guard. No server-side HTML scraping is required.
2. **Catalog & Search**: Direct client queries to TMDB API v3 with public API key `8476a7ab80ad76f0936744df0430e67c` for catalog carousels, genre/year/provider filters, and multi-search (`/3/search/multi`). Supplementary curated lists via `https://lists.wing.st/joy`.
3. **Subtitles & Skip Timestamps**: 280+ multilingual subtitles per title via `https://subs.wing.st/subtitles` (proxying SRT files) and intro/credit timestamps via `https://api.theintrodb.org/v2/media`.
4. **Cryptographic Stream Resolution Protocol (`lumen-gate-v2`)**: Reverse engineered and verified end-to-end in Node.js. Uses standalone WebAssembly `crush.wasm` (`seal_request`) to seal requests to `POST https://api.wing.st/g`, and decrypts the response with Web Crypto AES-256-GCM.
5. **Media Delivery & Codecs**: Clear unencrypted HLS v7 from `https://lightspeed.st/hls/*` delivering 360p, 720p, 1080p H.264/AAC streams and 4K HEVC Main 10 PQ streams disguised as `.png` fMP4 chunks (`init.png`, `seg-v*.png`).
6. **Critical webOS Feasibility Finding**: `lightspeed.st` strictly enforces `Origin: https://cinejoy.pk` and returns HTTP 404 on `file://` or missing Origin. A lightweight local Node.js proxy server (listening on `http://127.0.0.1:8088`) is required to rewrite the Origin and Referer headers for HLS manifest and segment requests.
